**The meaning of the verses**
﴿فَأَمَّا الْإِنسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ﴾ ﴿وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ﴾

As for man, when his Lord tests him with blessings, gives him plenty of provision and puts him in the best of living, he thinks this is because he is honoured by his Lord, and says: "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he thinks this is because he is of no worth to Allah, and says: "My Lord has humiliated me."

﴿كَلَّا ۖ بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ﴾ ﴿وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ﴾

The matter is not as this man thinks. Rather, honour comes through obeying Allah, and humiliation through disobeying Him. And you do not honour the orphan, whose father died while he was small, nor treat him well, nor do you urge one another to feed the needy person who does not have what is enough for him and meets his needs, …

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Amjad say that Allah loves them more than everyone else? And what did he say when the hail struck their field?
2. What did Umm Ma'n say to her son when his father died?
3. Is a poor person, or someone struck by hardship, someone Allah is angry with? And is a rich person loved by Allah because of his wealth? (Neither one; both are a test, and honour comes through obeying Allah, and part of that is honouring the orphan and feeding the poor.)

**This week's exercise**
This week your child sets aside part of what they have, from their pocket money or their sweets, for an orphan or a family in need, and delivers it with you themselves. And whenever something makes them happy or sad, they say, "Alhamdulillah," and you ask together: What does Allah want to see from me now?
